This bar chart illustrates the “effect” values for six different language families across six different models. The horizontal axis represents language family, with categories labeled “IE-Baltic”, “IE-Germanic”, “IE-Indic”, “IE-Romance”, “IE-Slavic”, “IE-other”, “Isolate”, “Semitic”, and “Uralic”, presented in that order. The vertical axis is labeled “effect” and displays a linear scale ranging from 0 to 30, with tick marks at intervals of 5. There are six sets of grouped bars for each language family, each representing a different model: “mBERT-L2” (black), “XLM-L2” (blue), “mBERT-R2” (red), “XLM-R2” (green), “mBERT-B2” (teal), and “XLM-B2” (brown). Each bar within a group includes error bars extending above and below the bar. For the “IE-Baltic” family, the “mBERT-L2” bar is approximately 7, “XLM-L2” is around 8, “mBERT-R2” is about 9, “XLM-R2” is approximately 8, “mBERT-B2” is around 6, and “XLM-B2” is about 7. The bars generally show a similar height pattern across all language families, with the “mBERT-R2” model consistently having the tallest bars. The bars are not sorted by height or any other apparent criteria. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, outlining, or annotation.
